# Voyage to the Blue Planet

Voyage to the Blue Planet was a 2024 concert tour by the American rock band Weezer. It commemorated the 30th anniversary of the band's debut studio album, *Weezer* (commonly known as the Blue Album), which was performed in full at each show. The tour ran from September 4 to October 12, 2024, across North America, featuring supporting acts the Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr. A pro-shot concert film documenting a performance from the tour was released in October 2024 and received positive feedback for capturing the event's thematic elements.

The tour incorporated a space-themed narrative, framing the performances as a mission to save a dying "Blue Planet" through the power of the Blue Album. Reviews noted the tour's ability to engage diverse audiences, blending nostalgia with theatrical staging, though some described the storyline as lighthearted and whimsical rather than elaborate. With no major controversies reported, the tour highlighted Weezer's enduring appeal across generations.

**Key points:**
- **Duration and scope:** 24 shows in arenas and venues primarily in the United States and Canada.
- **Supporting acts:** The Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr., both of which had previously toured with Weezer.
- **Setlist structure:** A mix of hits from various albums, selections from *Pinkerton* (1996), and the complete Blue Album.
- **Thematic elements:** Space voyage storyline with video interludes, emphasizing fun and fan interaction.
- **Related media:** A concert film filmed in Boston, streamed online, and later made available on platforms like YouTube.

**Background** 
Weezer, formed in Los Angeles in 1992, released their self-titled debut album on May 10, 1994, produced by Ric Ocasek and released on DGC Records. The album achieved commercial success, peaking at number 16 on the Billboard 200 and eventually certified quadruple platinum in the United States . It featured singles such as "Undone – The Sweater Song," "Buddy Holly," and "Say It Ain't So," which contributed to the band's rise in the alternative rock scene .

The tour was announced on March 11, 2024, following teaser posts on social media beginning February 14 . Promotional materials included a space-themed trailer and website updates . Pre-sale tickets were offered to fan club members starting March 13, with general sales following . Additional shows were added due to demand, including a second date in Washington, D.C., on September 15 and a final show in Palm Desert, California, on October 12 .

**Concert film** 
A concert film titled *Weezer's Voyage to the Blue Planet: The Concert Film* was directed by Garrett Nicholson and filmed during the September 10, 2024, performance at TD Garden in Boston . It depicts the band's "mission" to heal the Blue Planet using the Blue Album, aligning with the tour's narrative . The film was initially streamed on October 13 and 14, 2024, via Moment.co, and later uploaded to YouTube in 4K resolution . It holds a user rating of 9.2 out of 10 on IMDb based on limited reviews .

**Reception** 
Critics and attendees described the tour as an effective celebration of the Blue Album, praising its nostalgic focus and audience engagement . One review highlighted the intergenerational crowd and the band's embrace of their quirky image, while noting the absence of high-energy elements like encores or mosh pits . Another emphasized the entertainment value, contrasting it with more artistic-oriented performances by contemporaries . Setlist.fm commentary called it a model for anniversary tours, citing its dynamic and fun execution .

Voyage to the Blue Planet was a concert tour by the American rock band Weezer, held in 2024 to mark the 30th anniversary of their debut album, *Weezer* (The Blue Album). The tour featured full performances of the album, accompanied by a fictional space-adventure storyline presented through video segments and stage design. It spanned 24 dates across North American arenas from September 4 to October 12, 2024, with the Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr. as opening acts. A companion concert film was released later that year, documenting the thematic and musical elements of the shows. The tour received generally positive responses for its nostalgic appeal and fan-focused approach, drawing crowds of varying ages and reinforcing Weezer's place in alternative rock history.

## Background

Weezer was formed in Los Angeles, California, in February 1992 by vocalist and guitarist Rivers Cuomo, drummer Patrick Wilson, guitarist Jason Cropper (later replaced by Brian Bell), and bassist Matt Sharp (later replaced by Scott Shriner in 2001). Their debut album, *Weezer* (The Blue Album), was recorded in 1993 and released on May 10, 1994, under DGC Records. Produced by former Cars frontman Ric Ocasek, the album blended power pop, alternative rock, and emo influences, achieving significant commercial and critical success. It reached number 16 on the U.S. Billboard 200 chart and has sold over 3.3 million copies in the United States, earning quadruple platinum certification from the Recording Industry Association of America . Key tracks include "My Name Is Jonas," "Buddy Holly," and "Only in Dreams," which helped establish the band's signature sound of catchy melodies paired with introspective lyrics .

By 2024, Weezer had released 15 studio albums and maintained a dedicated fanbase, despite mixed critical reception to some later works. The Voyage to the Blue Planet tour was conceived as a commemoration of the Blue Album's milestone, building on previous anniversary events like a 2019 performance of the album in full at the Memories Tour . Teasers for the tour began on social media on February 14, 2024, with cryptic posts about a "voyage" . The full announcement came on March 11, 2024, via a space-themed promotional video and updates to the band's website, evoking science fiction aesthetics to tie into the "Blue Planet" concept—symbolizing Earth and the album's blue cover .

In August 2024, select fans received promotional packages containing a musical greeting card that played "Buddy Holly" endlessly, a sticker reading "You Just Got Weezered," and a cassette tape with narration by Cuomo previewing the tour, followed by early demo tracks . Ticket pre-sales for fan club members and other groups started on March 13, 2024, with high demand leading to sold-out shows and additions to the itinerary . The tour followed Weezer's joint UK dates with the Smashing Pumpkins earlier in 2024 and preceded planned 2025 performances in Europe, the UK, and festivals .

## Overview

The tour adopted a narrative framework where Weezer portrayed astronauts on a mission to revive a dying "Blue Planet" threatened by an alien antagonist named Bokkus. Video interludes depicted the band's shuttle, Betsy 2.0, navigating space, encountering obstacles like the "Pinkerton asteroid belt," and ultimately restoring the planet by performing the Blue Album . This storyline was integrated into the stage production, with screens showing animated sequences, including a faux news report at the start and credits at the end . The theme extended to merchandise and fan interactions, fostering a playful, immersive atmosphere .

Supporting acts the Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr. were selected for their prior collaborations with Weezer and complementary styles—the Flaming Lips for their psychedelic performances and Dinosaur Jr. for their alternative rock roots . The Flaming Lips' sets included hits from albums like *The Soft Bulletin* and *Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots*, often involving audience participation . Dinosaur Jr. provided energetic openers, setting a tone of 1990s nostalgia .

Notable events included rapid sell-outs, such as the September 14, 2024, show in Washington, D.C., prompting an additional date the following day . The final added show on October 12 in Palm Desert, California, extended the tour slightly beyond its initial schedule . No cancellations or major disruptions were reported, and the production emphasized accessibility, with arenas chosen for their capacity to host large, diverse crowds .

## Set list

The set list was structured around the tour's narrative, beginning with modern tracks and hits, transitioning through songs from *Pinkerton*, and culminating in the full Blue Album. This format allowed for a build-up to the anniversary focus while showcasing the band's evolution . Variations occurred minimally across shows, with the core remaining consistent .

No encores were performed, with shows averaging 1 hour and 36 minutes . During "Undone – The Sweater Song," Cuomo often encouraged audience participation by letting fans sing lyrics . At the Boston show, Cuomo noted a rare mosh pit during "Only in Dreams," remarking on its uniqueness in the band's 30-year history .

## Concert film

*Weezer's Voyage to the Blue Planet: The Concert Film* was directed by Garrett Nicholson and produced with an estimated budget of $15 . Filmed at the TD Garden in Boston on September 10, 2024, it captures the full performance, including the space narrative and audience interactions . The film portrays Weezer's journey to "heal" the Blue Planet with the Blue Album's music, incorporating animated elements and the band's commentary . It was first streamed live on Moment.co on October 13 and 14, 2024, and subsequently released on YouTube in 4K . As of late 2024, it held a 9.2/10 rating on IMDb from 15 users . The production highlighted the tour's whimsical aspects, such as Cuomo planting a flag with the band's logo on the "planet" stage .

## Reception

The tour was well-received for its celebration of the Blue Album and ability to attract a broad audience, from longtime fans to younger listeners influenced by social media . Attendees appreciated the nostalgic setlist and the band's unpretentious stage presence, which aligned with their "losercore" image . The space theme was described as corny yet endearing, enhancing the fun without overshadowing the music . Reviews praised the integration of *Pinkerton* tracks, noting stronger crowd reactions to them in some venues .

One college newspaper review called it a unifying experience for generations, emphasizing Weezer's dedication despite self-deprecating lyrics in their catalog . Another highlighted the entertainment focus, contrasting it with more serious rock acts, and noted the well-balanced sound mixing . Setlist.fm analysis deemed it an exemplary anniversary tour, effective in delivering beauty, power, and dynamism . Criticisms were minor, including the lack of encores and occasional over-earnest audience prompts from openers . Overall, the tour reinforced Weezer's cultural staying power, with no significant negative feedback or incidents reported .

**Voyage to the Blue Planet** was [Weezer's](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer "Weezer") headlining [2024](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=2024 "2024") North American tour, occurring from [September 4](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=September_4 "September 4") to [October 12](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=October_12 "October 12"). [The Flaming Lips](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=The_Flaming_Lips "The Flaming Lips") and [Dinosaur Jr.](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_Jr. "Dinosaur Jr.") were the opening acts. To celebrate the 30th anniversary of _[Weezer (The Blue Album)](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_, the album was played in full at each show.

Overview
--------

Social media posts teasing a "voyage" were first shared on [February 14](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=February_14 "February 14"), [2024](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=2024 "2024").[[1]](https://www.weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet#cite_note-1) The tour was formally announced on [March 11](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=March_11 "March 11"), accompanied by a space-themed trailer video and website redesign. A new [Weezer Fan Club](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_Fan_Club "Weezer Fan Club") membership bundle and a [one-off anniversary performance](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_03/15/2024 "Weezer concert: 03/15/2024") at [Club Dump](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Club_Dump "Club Dump") were also announced. _[Weezer (The Blue Album)](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_ was set to be performed at each show in full to celebrate the album's 30th anniversary, alongside "[other] Weezer songs, rarities, and more." [The Flaming Lips](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=The_Flaming_Lips "The Flaming Lips") and [Dinosaur Jr.](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Dinosaur_Jr. "Dinosaur Jr."), who have both performed with Weezer previously, were announced as the tour's opening bands.[[2]](https://www.weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://www.weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet#cite_note-3)

On [March 14](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=March_14 "March 14"), only one day after pre-sale tickets became available to fan club members and other select groups, the [September 14](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=September_14 "September 14")[show in Washington, DC](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_09/14/2024 "Weezer concert: 09/14/2024") sold out. In response, an [additional show](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_09/15/2024 "Weezer concert: 09/15/2024") at the same venue on the following day was added to the tour schedule.[[4]](https://www.weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet#cite_note-4) Another [additional show in Palm Desert, California](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer_concert:_10/12/2024 "Weezer concert: 10/12/2024") on [October 12](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=October_12 "October 12") was added in June.[[5]](https://www.weezerpedia.com/wiki/Voyage_to_the_Blue_Planet#cite_note-5)

In August, roughly two weeks before the beginning of the tour, an unknown quantity of promotional packages were sent to random fans. These contained a musical gag card, a sticker, and an unmarked white cassette. The card was produced by Joker Greeting and plays "[Buddy Holly](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Buddy_Holly "Buddy Holly")" continuously when opened. It additionally ejects confetti when an enclosed string is pulled. The sticker features an illustration of the _[Blue Album](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer\_(The\_Blue\_Album) "Weezer (The Blue Album)")_ artwork and the text "You Just Got Weezered". The cassette, housed in a blank blue J-card, contains narration by [Rivers Cuomo](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Rivers_Cuomo "Rivers Cuomo") previewing the upcoming tour, followed by the entirety of [Weezer's third demo](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Weezer%27s_third_demo "Weezer's third demo") (not including "[Surf Wax America](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Surf_Wax_America "Surf Wax America")").

Story
-----

A breaking news report informs the audience that the Blue Planet is dying, and that Weezer is being sent to restore it. They board the [Betsy 2.0](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Betsy_2.0 "Betsy 2.0"), a shuttle which that will take them and the audience on a dangerous voyage to save the Blue Planet. The lights brighten and shows the shuttle heading up for lift off, with fans cheering the group on. As the band plays, the big screen shows Betsy flying through space, travelling through a Weezer-themed space bar and running into the alien [Bokkus](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Bokkus "Bokkus"), who has a hatred of the group. During a trek through the _[Pinkerton](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Pinkerton "Pinkerton")_ asteroid belt, Bokkus drains Betsy's shields by hurling pies and other objects at the shuttle. The shuttle crashes, which launches [M1](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=M1 "M1") to look for parts as the band plays cuts from the titular album. After the fourth part is found, the shuttle takes off for the Blue planet.

The planet is found, but its dying and requires _the Blue Album_ to come back to life. [Rivers Cuomo](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Rivers_Cuomo "Rivers Cuomo") plants a flag adorned with the [Flying =W=](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Flying_%3DW%3D "Flying =W=") in the ground, and the band performs the entire album front-to-back. The planet is shown coming back to life, with grass, trees and buildings growing as they perform. The band lands at the Blue Rocks Amphitheater and are cheered on by the planet's native population of Weezeroids, a species which Cuomo and the crowd are members of. Bokkus finds the ampitheatre and attacks with laser cannons, only to be defeated by loud speakers and the Weezeroids' laser eyes. After the credits roll, a faux news report similar to the one at the beginning of the show plays where Cuomo states that the mission has inadvertently opened up a wormhole and altered the timeline (for example, changing Rivers' name to [Kurt](https://www.weezerpedia.com/w/index.php?title=Kurt_Cobain "Kurt Cobain")), and that they need to fix it before any more damage is caused.

5.title: ONE NIGHT OF NO SHAME - Weezer: Voyage to the Blue Planet Review | Concert Reviews
5.description: Weezer are not looking to create high art. They are the only crowd-pleasing rock band from the past thirty years still left on the touring circuit. I had limited knowledge …
5.content:
#### Weezer are not looking to create high art. They are the only crowd-pleasing rock band from the past thirty years still left on the touring circuit. I had limited knowledge of the tour before entering Moody Center on September 27th; what I had seen was an Instagram reel where Rivers Cuomo, the band’s frontman, planted the band’s flag on a moon landing stage set.

### _“One small step for man, one giant leap for Weezer-kind.”_

#### Though I was up in the nosebleeds, there was plenty of Weezer-kind on display. Behind me, there was one couple nuzzling each other and screaming all of the lyrics (_Pinkerton_ being their favorite album). In front of me was a father and mother, scolding their kids and snapping at them for standing up while dancing to “Beverly Hills.” It was fun for the whole family.

#### When The Flaming Lips, the opener, came on, I cheered. I had grown up with the band on the Spongebob movie soundtrack and through their two most lauded albums, _The Soft Bulletin_ and _Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots_. Wayne Coyne’s voice has aged gracefully, but his constant pleas to the audience to clap and sing along before - and even during - some of their hit songs came across as less ironic and punk, and more desperate.

#### Weezer killed throughout the entire show, even during songs that only die-hard fans knew the lyrics to. The audience quieted during the theatrical sections in between songs, displaying retro 3D models of aliens flying around monochromatic planetoids.

#### The “Buddy Holly” riff was present. Their eponymous 1994 _Blue Album_ was the focus of the set, but most of the audience danced and head banged to their sophomore album, _Pinkerton_. Rivers flaunted a pick slide during a solo, and at last, I felt I was at the big rock n’ roll show that movies and TV shows had promised.

#### “Undone” stood out as the most interesting live performance of the night. Rivers became a showman, letting the audience fill in the lyrics during some of the choruses. His self-pitying whine has tapped the Id of the nation. Despite the variety in material across Weezer’s 30 year catalog, the band sounded exactly as they do on their studio albums. It was also extremely well mixed, jumping from muddy grunge-inspired tracks to dead-silent mid-2000s cuts. They were all well-structured rock songs, typically up-tempo. The night ranged more in dynamics than anything else. How quiet the guitars were told the audience how far from the ‘90s the piece was written.

#### I went into the concert trying to avoid the thought that I am, in fact, a Weezer fan. My friends were always playing their 2021 album, _OK Human_, in high school. I bought the blue album on CD as a gift for one of these friends, but ended up giving it to him a month later. In the meantime, I used it on my clock radio as an alarm. I woke up every morning to the first thirty seconds of “Undone”. I thought I was too smug, smart, and interested in jazz to be enjoying Weezer in public. Sure, maybe I wasn’t as big of a fan as the people around me, but I still bought a T-shirt and had a solid time at a rock show. I suppose finding that comfort in being a nerd was what the night was all about.

4.title: Keepin’ it weezy: “Voyage to the Blue Planet” tour review
4.description: Honestly, they don’t look like much: four middle-aged white dudes brandishing sticker-adorned guitars and glasses, with only slight smiles suggesting any form of excitement (despite arriving on the stage via prop spaceship). With no backup dancers, no jumping around on stage, no crowd surfing or mosh pit – they still managed to pack the stadium...
4.content:
[![Image 1: Weezer on Xcel Center stage.](https://themacweekly.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Screenshot-2024-09-12-at-11.36.48%E2%80%AFPM-1200x901.png)](https://themacweekly.com/83177/arts/keepin-it-weezy-voyage-to-the-blue-planet-tour-review/#photo)

Weezer on Xcel Center stage.

Honestly, they don’t look like much: four middle-aged white dudes brandishing sticker-adorned guitars and glasses, with only slight smiles suggesting any form of excitement (despite arriving on the stage via prop spaceship). With no backup dancers, no jumping around on stage, no crowd surfing or mosh pit – they still managed to pack the stadium to its very brim, nostalgia palpable as the audience screams. Standing still with no choreography or fanservice, Weezer began to play – nay, _shred_– much to fans’ delight. These unassuming nerds are guys you’d probably pass any other day on the street, and they’re putting on a hell of a show.

This is the dichotomy of the rock band Weezer, caught between a memed-to-death “losercore” reputation and critically acclaimed widespread appeal across multiple generations. On our way to the Xcel Center — Weezer’s venue of choice for kicking off their “Voyage to the Blue Planet” tour on Sept. 4 — the cross-generational draw of the band became staggeringly apparent. Lining the streets and the halls of the stadium were millennials holding craft IPAs and matching their flannels to their “Blue Album” shirts, Gen Xers groaning about concession prices with their apathetic teenage children and Gen Z nerds – ourselves included – in Converse, Hot Topic cargo pants and thrifted oversized button- downs, stepping into the concert with a knowing self-awareness for the band’s reputation.

The reactions we got telling people about our plans for the evening ranged from judgmental eyebrow raises and laughter to sincere jealousy. To us, Weezer stands in a gray area of pop culture, with its fans expressing both tongue-in-cheek support and genuine love for the band.

To be fair, the dorky reputation the band has garnered is not without reason: the concert had its own (somewhat ridiculous) plot, a space drama (maybe, we hypothesized, inspired by the lead singer Rivers Cuomo’s own idea for a space-themed rock opera he had in the 90s!) complete with corny cutscenes about needing to “save the blue planet” by playing the entirety of the “Blue Album.” According to the show’s overarching story, Rivers Cuomo is an alien and so are all of us in the audience: the Weezeroids.

But this loose plot was nothing compared to the driving force of the music. The openers The Flaming Lips and Dinosaur Jr first brought energy into the crowd, but Weezer seemed to take it to another level. They started with some hits from their other albums – familiar radio-friendly numbers like “Island in the Sun,” “Beverly Hills” and “Pork and Beans.” After this, much to our surprise (and extreme joy), they moved on to songs from their second album “Pinkerton,” a cult favorite among fans, with a whopping four songs in a row: “Pink Triangle,” “Getchoo,” “Why Bother” and “Across the Sea”. Considering how many of the songs they played have been a public source of shame for Cuomo with their angsty and somewhat juvenile lyrics from his college days, it was a real treat to hear them live.

After these “classics,” they moved to start playing all of the “Blue Album,” kicking the songs off by claiming “the blue planet” as their own, as “one small step for Weezer, one giant leap for Weezerkind!” Here, the audience’s energy multiplied, with recognizable tunes like “Buddy Holly,” “Say It Ain’t So” and “Undone: The Sweater Song” hyping up old and new fans alike. And, in true Weezer fashion, there was no encore nor particularly flashy goodbye: only all six-plus minutes of “Only in Dreams” and a quick, humble thank you and farewell.

But, throughout the concert, we were mostly surprised by how much we knew by heart: even some of the more “deep cuts” had us dancing and singing in our seats just as much as the hits. Although we had found Weezer in different ways – with one of us growing up listening to Weezer in her dad’s car and one of us doing a discography deep-dive during the COVID-19 pandemic – we both shared with each other our fond memories associated with the band, phases in our lives where one specific song was our particular favorite, and the most out-of-pocket lyrics we’ve grown to laugh at and even relate to. It may sometimes be embarrassing to find Cuomo’s words relatable, but it is this very tension that makes being a Weezer fan worthwhile; the fanbase shares and revels in this awkwardness.

All this is to say that there is no one stereotype of a Weezer fan. Sure, it can be hard to overlook the TikTok jokes about it being “incel music,” the iconic “Buddy Holly” riff and (to be fair) the music they’ve released that’s pure garbage (“Raditude,” no matter how ironically you spin it, is an objectively horrible collection of music). But behind that façade of irony lies a band with a dedication to their music, a full embracement of their past rarely seen by other artists, and a deeply passionate fandom from all walks of life. As we listened to the music, sandwiched next to a Millennial couple and a Gen X skater, it became clear Weezer has something for everyone of all ages.

So, although that mosh pit was the stillest one we had ever seen, the overwhelming love radiating from every seat in that stadium made clear the impact of Weezer’s music on us all. Through all the canned dialogue and guitar solos, Weezer managed to unite thousands of people in the stadium and millions around the world, with authenticity and heartfelt energy.

### Event Info

Weezer is an American rock band formed in Los Angeles, CA in 1992, currently consisting of Rivers Cuomo (lead vocals, lead guitar), Patrick Wilson (drums), Brian Bell (rhythm guitar, backing vocals, keyboards), and Scott Shriner (bass, backing vocals). Weezer has sold 10 million albums in the U.S., and over 35 million records worldwide. Their catalogue has included such megahits as “Buddy Holly,” “Undone (The Sweater Song),” “Say It Ain’t So,” “El Scorcho,” “Hash Pipe,” “Island In The Sun,” “Beverly Hills,” “Pork and Beans,” and more. Weezer has won Grammys, MTV Video Music Awards, and more throughout their career. Following massively acclaimed album releases in 2016 and 2017 (Weezer [The White Album] and Pacific Daydream, respectively), and two sold out amphitheater tours with Panic! At the Disco (in 2016) and Pixies (in 2018), Weezer released a fan-inspired cover of Toto’s “Africa.” The cover propelled the band back into the charts across the board, giving Weezer their FIFTH #1, TENTH Top 5, and SIXTEENTH Top 10 at Alternative Radio, in addition to landing Top 5 on the Hot AC chart. It has since gone Platinum. They then surprise dropped a covers album at the start of 2019 -- Weezer (The Teal Album) -- which has been streamed over a hundred million times since its release. In 2021, Weezer released two very different but equally Weezer albums – OK Human, an orchestral pop album meditating on technology and disconnectedness, and Van Weezer, an homage to the band’s shared metal roots growing up. OK Human’s first single, “All My Favorite Songs,” was one of the biggest rock hits of 2021, and was subsequently nominated for a Grammy for “Best Rock Song.” In 2022, the band released SZNZ, a four EP project inspired by Vivaldi’s Four Seasons, and completed the European leg of the Hella Mega tour, which sold out stadiums in America throughout the year prior. In 2023, the band embarked on an incredible sold-out run across North America called the Indie Rock Road Trip, which was hailed as one of the best tours of the summer.

*   **Categories:**[On Tour Now](https://www.setlist.fm/news/on-tour-now)[General News](https://www.setlist.fm/news/general-news)**Tagged:**[Weezer](https://www.setlist.fm/setlists/weezer-33d6a4f9.html "More Weezer setlists")[Dinosaur Jr.](https://www.setlist.fm/setlists/dinosaur-jr-1bd6895c.html "More Dinosaur Jr. setlists")[The Flaming Lips](https://www.setlist.fm/setlists/the-flaming-lips-43d6fb1f.html "More The Flaming Lips setlists")[The Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour](https://www.setlist.fm/search?artist=33d6a4f9&tour=43dcaf03 "The Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour by Weezer setlists")

Of all the anniversary tours countless bands have embarked on, Weezer's Voyage to the Blue Planet Tour just may be the best.

Celebrating the 30th trip around the sun of their debut LP, the _Blue Album_, the quartet has mindfully created an excellent setlist, invited amazing opening acts, and created a video presentation that keeps you riveted.

And of course, the songs are nostalgic, delightful, and wholesome.

![Image 4: The band Weezer is promoting their Voyage to the Blue Planet tour in a promo shot featuring them dressed in white astronaut suits](https://media.cdn.setlistfm.com/news/2024-06/1719563941953/Weezer_BluePlanet_BusBench_finalv2.jpg)

Weezer are the anti-rock stars who can magically fill up seemingly any venue they want on the strength of a deep catalogue starting with their first two records.

As great as the quartet are, the fun comes from singing along to Rivers' sweet lyrics - not from some crazy stage show. That's where The Flaming Lips come in - a band who wants to trip you out, or more accurately, provide the lights and sounds for you as you trip balls.

Something Weezer themselves seem to be venturing into a tiny bit with their highly produced video background elements.

Kicking the show off is J. Mascis' Dinosaur Jr. who just might be the best guitarist in rock, and if not that, the loudest and gnarliest.

Both openers are excellent extensions of what one might imagine are the band's fondest hopes and wishes: to rock supremely, and a little oddly.

If indeed that was the goal for the 30th, consider Voyage to the Blue Planet a mission accomplished.

It's beautiful, powerful, dynamic, and fun.

![Image 5: Weezer's setlist in The Anthem, Washington, DC, USA, on September 15, 2024, showing 26 songs and some songs are tour debuts](https://media.cdn.setlistfm.com/large/news/2024-09/1726560946154/Screenshot%202024-09-17%20at%203.15.19%E2%80%AFAM.png)

Weezer's set is arranged the way others should take note of. It begins with a pair of deep cuts from another album celebrating an anniversary, 2014's _Everything Will Be Alright in the End_.

Those lead into four familiar numbers that get everyone singing along. And at Sunday's show in Washington DC's The Anthem, the band inserted the delightful "All My Favorite Songs" from 2021's _OK Human_.

After four more tunes, the band did the absolutely correct thing. They played five songs from the follow up to the _Blue_ album, _Pinkerton,_ depending on who you talk to, the band's greatest album ever.

The five songs that preclude the Blue Album is called The Pinkerton Asteroid Belt

After performing that little mini-set the band played the entire Blue album from beginning to end.

The video screen tell the adventure of the group in a fun and funny narrative.

It's a video game, a movie, and a rock show all in one with the best sound.

"May they never fall out of orbit," [_Variety_ wrote](https://variety.com/2024/music/concert-reviews/weezer-blue-album-new-york-concert-review-1236142876/ "https://variety.com/2024/music/concert-reviews/weezer-blue-album-new-york-concert-review-1236142876/").

Weezer continues their tour through this month and next with stops at basketball arenas around North America. 

In November they headline a long night at the baseball stadium in Phoenix alongside Sublime, Third Eye Blind, and The Violent Femmes.
